summary: The English of 5:19-5:23 is faithful and follows Bartenura and Rambam throughout; no sentence of the English needs changing. The main faults are lexical: the senses were filled mechanically (mostly '1', often the entry heading or a name etymology), and many tokens are linked to the wrong homograph (place or personal names such as Ain, Tob, Rahab, Helek, Huppah, Agra, or the noun 'torrent' for the verb 'inherit'), which are relinked to the Jastrow entries in the pack or have their sense removed. Three commentary summaries misread the Hebrew (Bartenura's 'feed him like an ox', Rambam's zehirut as 'caution', Rambam's 'reproof of teachers'), and two grammar notes contradict the morphology (עַז as a noun, מֵת as a participle). The model morphology is largely sound; fixes are construct/emphatic states, numeral gender, a few lemmas and roots, and the gender of שַׁחַת.

With the perfects עָבַר and בָּטֵל, מֵת is read as the Qal perfect (as the morphology and the English have it): 'he had died', not the adjective 'dead'.

patches.value: מֵת: Qal perfect 3rd masc. sing. of the stative verb מות; the same form is also the participle/adjective 'dead'. Here it stands with two perfects: 'as if he had died'.
patches.reason: The old note called it an adjective/participle, against the morphology and the English.

value: The four animal similes are parallel, each of the form adjective + כְּ + animal: bold / leopard, light / eagle, swift / deer, strong / lion. A single purpose phrase, 'to do the will of your Father in Heaven', governs all four.

The second saying is an elliptical antithesis with no verb: 'bold of face (goes) to Gehinnom, shame of face to the Garden of Eden'. עַז פָּנִים and בֹּשֶׁת פָּנִים are construct chains: עַז is the adjective 'strong, bold' in the construct ('bold of face'), בֹּשֶׁת the noun 'shame' in the construct.
יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ is the standard petition formula ('may it be Your will') and shifts the form to second person address to God: 'Your city, Your Torah'.

שֶׁתִּבְנֶה is a purpose/content clause: 'that You build'. In the Mishnaic petition, the verb is in the imperfect after the formula; חֶלְקֵנוּ בְתוֹרָתֶךָ 'our portion in Your Torah' is the second request.
The words עַז כַּנָּמֵר, וְקַל כַּנֶּשֶׁר, וְרָץ כַּצְּבִי, וְגִבּוֹר כָּאֲרִי pair a trait with its image; the first plays on עַז as both 'fierce' and 'brazen' (cf. עַז פָּנִים below).
patches.reason: עַז is an adjective (bdbs:עַז (a), Jastrow 'strong, firm'), not the noun 'boldness' (that is עֹז).

value: Each stage is an elliptical clause of the form 'son of N (years) to X': the verb 'is fit' is understood. The ל prefix is 'for' (fit for, ready for).

The ages count by tens from twenty to a hundred; בֶּן שָׁנִים is a fixed idiom for age. Gender of the numerals follows the noun they do not name: שָׁנָה (feminine) takes חָמֵשׁ, עֶשֶׂר, שְׁלשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, etc.

Each ל-noun is a stage of life or a pursuit: מִקְרָא (Bible), מִשְׁנָה (oral teaching), מִצְוֹת (commandments), תַּלְמוּד (study), חֻפָּה (marriage), רדף (pursuit), כֹּחַ (strength), בִּינָה, עֵצָה, זִקְנָה, שֵׂיבָה, גְּבוּרָה, שׁוּחַ.

The last clause is a full sentence: כְּאִלּוּ מֵת וְעָבַר וּבָטֵל מִן הָעוֹלָם, with three Qal perfects (מֵת is the perfect of the stative מות): 'as if he had died and passed and ceased from the world'.
patches.reason: The note called מֵת a participle/adjective, contradicting the morphology and the English 'had died'.

value: The saying mixes Hebrew and Aramaic: הֲפֹךְ בָּהּ וַהֲפֹךְ בָּהּ is Hebrew; דְּכֹלָּא בָהּ וּבָהּ תֶּחֱזֵי וְסִיב וּבְלֵה בָהּ וּמִנַּהּ לֹא תָזוּעַ is Aramaic; שֶׁאֵין לְךָ מִדָּה טוֹבָה הֵימֶנָּה is Hebrew again.
The feminine בָּהּ refers back to the Torah, as the commentators say (the mishnah does not name it: it follows the previous saying).
The imperatives הֲפֹךְ, סִיב, בְּלֵה are paired: turn it over and over; grow old and wear out in it.
The negation לֹא תָזוּעַ is a prohibition in Aramaic style ('do not move'); the final clause gives the reason with שֶׁאֵין לְךָ 'for you have not'.
מִדָּה 'measure, quality'; the English 'quality' also allows 'virtue' or 'standard'.
patches.reason: Quote the base text: it reads לֹא, not לָא.

patches.value: Translation choices. עַיִן טוֹבָה / רָעָה are kept as the literal 'good eye' / 'evil eye', with the commentators' definitions (Bartenura, Rambam: contentment vs. greed) given in the notes. רוּחַ נְמוּכָה 'humble spirit', נֶפֶשׁ שְׁפָלָה 'modest soul' (Bartenura: restraint and abstinence from desires; Rambam: restraint (זְהִירוּת), above all in sexual matters), נֶפֶשׁ רְחָבָה 'broad soul' (great craving). אֹהֲבַי is 'those who love me' (Bartenura reads the verse as naming Abraham 'the lover', Isa 41:8). בְּאֵר שַׁחַת is 'the pit of destruction'; שַׁחַת is both 'pit' and 'destruction/corruption'. Gehinnom is left in Hebrew form per the decisions.
patches.reason: Rambam's זְהִירוּת is restraint from desire (his proofs are Abraham's not looking at Sarah, and his conduct with Hagar), not 'caution'.

patches.value: Rambam: a good eye is contentment (הַהִסְתַּפְּקוּת), a lowly soul is restraint from desire (הַזְּהִירוּת), a humble spirit is extra humility; their opposites are greed for money (evil eye), great lust (broad soul) and pride (haughty spirit). He finds each trait in Abraham (Gen 14:23; 12:11; 16:6; 21:11; 18:27) and in Balaam, and explains 'men of blood and deceit' of Balaam.
patches.reason: זְהִירוּת here is restraint from desire, as Rambam's examples (Sarah, Hagar) show, not 'caution'; הַחֲרִיצוּת לִקְנוֹת הַמָּמוֹן is avidity for wealth, not 'diligence'.

patches.value: Rambam: though he says 'the bold-faced to Gehinnom', he commands boldness for reproof, as teachers must reprove, and the like: use a vice in its place for God's will ('with the crooked be subtle'), on condition that the aim is truth, 'to do the will of your Father'. Shame is a gift to this nation (the seed of Abraham is bashful, merciful, kind); so he prays: as You granted us this trait, grant that Your city be rebuilt.
patches.reason: בְּתוֹכְחַת הַמּוֹרִים is the reproof that teachers give, not the rebuking of one's teachers; the summary 'boldness in rebuking teachers' reverses it. Proposed reading.

patches.value: Bartenura: five years for Scripture is learned from orlah (Lev 19:23-25): three years of nothing, the fourth year 'holy', when the father teaches the shape of the letters and the vowel points, and from the fifth 'you shall eat its fruit': from then on 'feed him (Torah) like an ox' (סְפֵי לֵיהּ כְּתוֹרָא).
patches.reason: סְפֵי לֵיהּ כְּתוֹרָא is 'stuff/feed him like an ox', not 'he is to be strengthened like an ox'.
כֹּל is a noun (BDB n-m; Jastrow), here in the construct before מִי, not an adjective.
שַׁחַת is feminine (bdbs n-f, Jastrow f.).
שַׁחַת is feminine (bdbs n-f, Jastrow f.).
In עַז פָּנִים the adjective is bound to פָּנִים: construct ('bold of face').
In בֹּשֶׁת פָּנִים the noun is bound to פָּנִים: construct ('shame of face').
גַן עֵדֶן is a construct chain: 'garden of Eden'.
מְהֵרָה is a noun 'haste' (bdbs n-f); בִּמְהֵרָה is 'in haste'. The adverb sense comes from the phrase, not the word.
With שָׁנִים (feminine) the numeral is the short form חָמֵשׁ, used with feminine nouns, and it is absolute (construct is חֲמֵשׁ).
עֶשֶׂר is the form used with feminine nouns (here שָׁנִים understood) and stands alone here: absolute, not construct.
